field_question: Is the Skinner Ridge sandstone block in place (lower Rockytop) or a float block (upper Rockytop)?
objective: Evaluate whether line of sight from the Option A standoff viewpoint (~22 m southwest) permits inspection of the basal contact interface to determine bedding continuity, or whether intervening topography obscures the contact.
assumptions: Observer eye height is 1.5 m above local ground surface.
Terrain elevation is bilinearly sampled from the primary 1 m USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE DTM.
Sightlines are straight rays connecting observer eye elevation to target top elevation.
Planetary curvature over ~22 m distance introduces < 0.1 mm vertical offset and is negligible.
Basal contact sits at ground level (target height 0.0 m).
Upper bedding and facies features sit at raised elevations (+0.5 m to +1.0 m).

target.name: Skinner Ridge block
target.description: Fine-to-medium grained laminated sandstone block (~1 m across) at the front of Jezero's western fan.

illustrative_standoff.label: Illustrative Option A standoff (~22 m SW, matching scope rough check)
illustrative_standoff.description: Offset southwest along the Option A approach terrain (~21.2 m - 22 m), matching the scope's 0.15 m obstruction check.

option_a_terminus.label: Option A outbound terminus (waypoint 26_1222, 21.77 m SW)
option_a_terminus.description: End-of-outbound traverse vertex for Option A, offset 21.77 m southwest from Skinner Ridge.

conclusion: Ground-level contact (height 0.0 m, basal contact) is obscured by topography from the Option A standoff viewpoint (~21-22 m southwest), resulting in ~0.07 m to ~0.15 m of obstruction along the intervening terrain crest (~18-19 m from the observer). Conversely, raised features (+0.5 m and +1.0 m) clear the crest with ~0.28 m to ~0.37 m of clearance at +0.5 m, and ~0.71 m to ~0.81 m clearance at +1.0 m. Consequently, an astronaut observing from Option A can view upper bedding layers and alternating protruding/recessive facies, but cannot determine basal contact continuity. The contact observation outcome from Option A must remain 'unresolved', and resolving origin requires direct physical inspection via route Option B.
